subject: Error with scaled precision in iid model

messages.author: cd8f249492ca9d15
messages.subject: Error with scaled precision in iid model
parts:
Hi - I'm getting a strange error when using the 'scale' argument with NA id's. Usually an NA drops the random effect from the model, which is useful for my model

Example below with INLA_22.05.07:

##
n = 10
df = data.frame(y = 1:10, id = c(1:(n - 1), NA), prec = 1)
inla(y ~ f(id, model = 'iid', scale = prec), data = df)

> Error in inla.ffield.section(file = file.ini, file.loc = file.loc, file.cov = file.cov,  :
  length(random.spec$values) == ns is not TRUE

Removing 'scale' resolves the issue. Setting the scale and/or outcome to be NA when id is NA doesn't solve the issue either.

Arie

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error with scaled precision in iid model
parts:
prec need to be a vector of the same length as id 

--

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error with scaled precision in iid model
parts:
Isn’t the issue here that while the length of the ID vector is 10, it only defines a size 9 iid effect?  So you need to set prec=rep(1, 9) in the f call.
Note that this means that prec shouldn’t be part of the observations data frame since it’s length is not directly related to the number of observations. It needs to be available in the evaluation environment for f() though. To be safe, you can  supply the whole data set as a list instead of a data.frame.

Finn
